title: Technical Writing Essentials, 2nd Edition: Designing Professional Communications in the Technical Fields
authors: Last, Suzan; Cojoc-Wisernig, Eduard; Gaudet, Loren; Lewis, Justin; Neveu, Candice; Saini, Sushil; Smith, Monika
summary: Second edition of Suzan Last's widely adopted technical writing text, covering reader-centred style, information design, teamwork, research, common technical genres, and public speaking. Adds new material on generative AI literacy, visual rhetoric, and a full part on user experience design.
notes: Edited by Suzan Last; individual chapters have their own author credits. Based on the 2019 first edition (pressbooks.bccampus.ca/technicalwriting). Only a PDF export was listed at time of check.

title: Technical Writing Essentials: Introduction to Professional Communications in the Technical Fields
summary: Introductory technical communication textbook built around audience and task analysis, concise reader-centred style, document design, teamwork, research methods, IEEE citation, and common workplace document types.
notes: Contributors: Candice Neveu, Monika Smith, Loren Gaudet. Superseded by the 2026 2nd edition but still online and widely cloned (e.g., UNH, NVCC, Seneca adaptations). Listed in the Open Textbook Library as CC BY. Some excerpts in the book carry their own permissions; check 'except where otherwise noted'.

title: Technical Writing Essentials - H5P Edition: Introduction to Professional Communications in the Technical Fields
summary: BCcampus adaptation of the 2019 Technical Writing Essentials that adds more than 40 interactive H5P self-check activities to the original chapters.
notes: Contributors: Candice Neveu, Monika Smith, Deb Nielsen. ISBN 978-1-77420-171-8. License statement: CC BY 4.0 except where otherwise noted.

title: Technical Writing Essentials: Introduction to Professional Communication in the Technical Fields (Seneca adaptation)
summary: Partial adaptation of Suzan Last's Technical Writing Essentials for Seneca Polytechnic, with interactive elements contributed by Tricia Hylton.
notes: Adapted from Suzan Last's original (pressbooks.bccampus.ca/technicalwriting). Year shown is the original's copyright year from metadata.

title: Technical Writing
authors: Gross, Allison; Hamlin, Annemarie; Merck, Billy; Rubio, Chris; Naas, Jodi; Savage, Megan; DeSilva, Michele
summary: Community-college technical writing text organized around producing a technical report: professional correspondence, audience analysis, proposals, information literacy, progress reports, graphics, ethics, report components, design, employment materials, and intercultural communication.
notes: Often cited as Hamlin, Rubio, and DeSilva (Open Oregon); current metadata lists seven authors. Adapted in part from David McMurrey's Online Technical Writing. ISBN 978-1-63635-065-3. LibreTexts mirror: Technical Writing (DeSilva et al.).

title: Open Technical Communication
authors: Tijerina, Tiffani (formerly Reardon); Powell, Tamara; Arnett, Jonathan; Logan, Monique; Race, Cassandra
summary: Kennesaw State's remix of McMurrey's Online Technical Writing and other open sources, covering technical genres, ethics, document design, writing process, usability testing, collaborative writing, technical editing, and basic HTML.
notes: Originally published 2016 (first titled Sexy Technical Communication) by Kennesaw State University; last major update 2020; no longer updated except for accessibility and broken links. Lead author now publishes as Tiffani Tijerina. Contributors include David McMurrey. Word/PDF zip available from the project page. A LibreTexts mirror (Open Technical Communication 3e) shows 'not declared' license; the OpenALG original is CC BY 4.0. The assignment brief listed authors as Reardon, Wright, Cook, Olsen; those names did not appear on any edition found.

title: Open Technical Communication, 2e
summary: Second edition of Open Technical Communication, reorganized into processes, applications, ethics and audience, and design, with new material on quoting, plagiarism, and using AI.
notes: Editors: Michelle Jimmerson and Jenny Rissen. Marked beta while funding is sought for additional chapters. Remix of David McMurrey's Online Technical Writing. Note license change from 1st edition (CC BY) to CC BY-NC-SA.

title: Online Technical Writing: Free Online Textbook for Technical Writing
summary: Long-running free technical writing textbook covering dozens of technical document types, information structures (description, process, definition, comparison), document design, and the writing process, with an extensive gallery of example documents.
notes: Continuously updated web textbook (copyright 1995-2026 per footer); formerly hosted at prismnet.com/~hcexres/textbook/. Source text for many other OER (Open Oregon Technical Writing, Open Technical Communication). LibreTexts mirror: Online Technical Writing (McMurrey).

title: Business Writing For Everyone
summary: Inclusive, process-oriented business writing text that uses storytelling (including a recurring narrative by Brenda Knights) to teach the decisions behind workplace genres, with H5P activities and reflection prompts.
notes: Each chapter opens with reflection questions and a narrative and ends with key takeaways and activities.

title: Communication at Work: A College-to-Career Guide to Success (Second Edition, 2026)
summary: College communications text organized in three units (communication fundamentals, applied writing, oral communication) that walks through a four-stage writing process and routine workplace genres, job applications, interpersonal and group communication, and presentations.
notes: Originally published 2019 (Algonquin College); editors Marieke Kalkhove and Geraldine Dion St. Pierre for the 2nd edition. Basis for many Canadian adaptations (Seneca, NSCC, Fanshawe).

title: NSCC Communication @ Work, 2nd Edition
authors: Krewenki, Condea; Munro, Judy; Smith, Jordan
summary: Nova Scotia Community College adaptation of Communication at Work for its COMM 2215 course, guiding students through workplace writing and speaking skills.
notes: Based on the first NSCC edition, which derives from Communication @ Work: Seneca College Edition (CC BY). Also mirrored at pressbooks.atlanticoer-relatlantique.ca.

title: Professional Communications: A Common Approach to Work-place Writing
summary: Fanshawe College's first-year common communications text in five units: communication foundations, the writing process, workplace communication, employment and interpersonal communication, and presentations and group work.
notes: Draws on Jordan Smith's Communication at Work and Melissa Ashman's Introduction to Professional Communications (credited in clones). Clone at pressbooks.nscc.ca/llscomm.

title: Advanced Professional Communication: A Principled Approach to Workplace Writing
summary: Second-level Fanshawe College text organized around principles of business messaging, style and format, social/cultural/employment communication, report and research writing, and visual, verbal, and group communication.
notes: Built on Professional Communications: A Common Approach to Work-place Writing (llscomm).

title: Technical and Professional Writing Genres: A Study in Theory and Practice
authors: Beilfuss, Michael; Bettes, Staci; Peterson, Katrina
summary: Two-part text pairing theory (audience, collaboration, ethics, document design) with practice chapters on the main workplace genres: correspondence, job applications, instructions, proposals, research, analytical reports, and oral reports.
notes: Editors: Eric Howerton and Katie Rieger. Each chapter has its own author credit.

title: Technical Writing @ SLCC
authors: Department of English, Linguistics, and Writing Studies at SLCC
summary: Course text for SLCC's ENGL 2100 that combines a six-step writing process with discipline-specific introductions to writing in the sciences, engineering, and computer science, plus sections on citation and copyright, corporate culture, civic engagement, and project planning.
notes: Includes 'Tips for Writing Tutors' sections. The computer science section covers requirements documents and software requirements specifications.

title: Communication for Business Professionals (Canadian Edition)
summary: Canadian adaptation of an open business communication text covering the communication process, delivering messages, audience, business writing genres, and presentations.
notes: Editor: Jenni Hayman; contributors David Simon, Michelle Grimes, Shauna Roch.

title: Professional Communications (Ontario adaptation)
authors: Dingwall, J.R.; Labrie, Chuck; McLennon, Trecia; Underwood, Laura
summary: Ontario adaptation, with H5P activities, of the Olds College Professional Communications OER, organized into modules on foundations (audience, channels, plain language, visuals, feedback), writing, presentations, and interpersonal communication.
notes: Adapted in 2018 by Wendy Ward (Niagara College) with eCampusOntario. The original Olds College version is at https://pressbooks.pub/dingwall/ (reported as CC BY 4.0 there; that site blocked automated license checks this session).

title: Fundamentals of Engineering Technical Communications: A Resource & Writing Guide for the Fundamentals of Engineering Program
authors: Wahlin, Leah (editor); FE & FEH Instructional Team
summary: Writing style guide for first-year engineering students that parallels the writing process with the engineering design process and covers style, visuals, lab reports and memos, executive summaries, progress reports, formatting, and presentations, with short exercises.
notes: Back matter includes ten short exercises (audience, word choice, data, graphs).

title: A Guide to Technical Communications: Strategies & Applications
summary: Textbook for Ohio State's second-level Engineering Technical Communications courses, grounding technical communication in rhetoric and covering job search, workplace and public communication, research reports, visual design, team projects, and presentations.
notes: Contributors: Deborah Kuzawa, Jennifer L. Herman, Yvonne Heather Burry. Listed in the Open Textbook Library.

title: Accessibility Toolkit - 2nd Edition
authors: Coolidge, Amanda; Doner, Sue; Robertson, Tara; Gray, Josie
summary: Practical guide for authors, instructional designers, and instructors on making open textbooks accessible, covering content types such as images, tables, links, formulas, multimedia, and font and colour choices.
notes: Editors: Lauri Aesoph, Josie Gray. First edition 2015. Useful as a student reading in technical editing or document accessibility units as well.

title: Open Professional and Technical Editing with Handbook
authors: Tijerina, Tiffani; Crumby, Mara; Anderson, Amber; Steele, Abigail; Darden, Hannah; Peterson, Harmony; Brown, Olivia
summary: Open textbook for technical and workplace editing courses covering markup, soft-copy and AI-assisted editing, sentence-level style, structural editing, document design, accessibility, visuals, style guides, and collaborative editing, with a grammar handbook for editors.
notes: Developed through a multi-class open pedagogy project with student co-authors at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock.

title: Technical Communication Across the Professions: An OER Textbook for TCID 3080 at UCCS
summary: University of Colorado Colorado Springs course text in four units: designing for a specific audience, plain language and technical style, technical and professional genres, and ethics.
notes: Listed in the UMN Manifold technical and professional communication OER collection.

title: Rhetorical Strategies for Workplace Communication: Professional and Technical Writing
summary: University of Arkansas text for professional and technical writing courses that approaches workplace genres through rhetorical strategy.
notes: Listed in the Open Textbook Library. Table of contents not reviewed in detail this session.

title: Writing for Strategic Communication Industries
summary: Practical writing text for public relations, advertising, and journalism students covering media writing conventions and AP-influenced style, ethics, news value, news and feature writing, PR writing, media relations, social media messaging, and portfolios.
notes: Author listed as Jasmine Roberts in the Open Textbook Library; editor Lynne Bonenberger.

title: Business Communication for Success
authors: [Author removed at request of original publisher]
summary: Comprehensive business communication text covering written and oral communication: the communication process, audience, preparing and revising business writing, routine and negative messages, reports, presentations, and intercultural communication.
notes: Adapted from a 2010 work whose publisher asked not to be credited. The Open Textbook Library says the UMN edition has been removed from its collection and points to Saylor and LibreTexts versions; the UMN Pressbooks site still answered at time of check. A Grand Valley State adaptation is at pressbooks.pub/unsw.

title: Howdy or Hello? Technical and Professional Communication (2nd Edition, Manifold Version)
authors: McKinney, Matt; Pattison, Kalani; LeMire, Sarah; Anders, Kathy; Hagstrom-Schmidt, Nicole
summary: Texas A&M's ENGL 210 textbook covering the rhetorical situation, workplace and research ethics, persuasion, style, organization, design, graphics, process, research and citation, collaboration, oral communication, correspondence, job applications, instructions, proposals, and informational and recommendation reports.
notes: Copyright 2025 per Manifold page; the 2nd edition was first issued on Pressbooks in 2021 (PDF of Pressbooks version at the OAKTrust handle). The older Pressbooks URLs (odp.library.tamu.edu/howdyorhello, pressbooks.library.tamu.edu/howdyorhello) blocked automated checks this session. Listed in the Open Textbook Library as CC BY-NC-SA.

title: Open Technical Writing: An Open-Access Text for Instruction in Technical and Professional Writing
summary: Situation-driven technical writing text that rejects one-size-fits-all report templates and instead teaches students to map and research a writing situation before choosing forms and approaches.
notes: PDF is 27.2 MB. LibreTexts mirror exists (Open Technical Writing (Pope)).

title: Introduction to Technical Writing: A Rhetorical Approach
publisher_platform: Pennsylvania Alliance for Design of Open Textbooks (PA-ADOPT)
summary: Short assignment-driven technical writing text in which each chapter teaches one skill (summarizing, visualizing, persuading) through a writing assignment, a student sample, and a rubric: a patent summary, a warning sign, and a recommendation report.
notes: First edition; file updated November 2025. Useful for its paired assignments and rubrics.

title: Web Writing
publisher_platform: Pennsylvania Alliance for Design of Open Textbooks (PA-ADOPT)
summary: Rhetorical approach to web writing and content strategy for advanced writing students, covering writing for specific online spaces and discourse communities and collecting and analyzing social media data to inform content strategy.
notes: First edition. Three chapters: introduction to web writing; web writing with the rhetorical situation; content strategy and content management.

title: Effective Professional Communication: A Rhetorical Approach
authors: Bennetch, Rebekah; Owen, Corey; Keesey, Zachary
summary: University of Saskatchewan professional communication text that teaches rhetorical theory and then applies it to technical writing basics, correspondence, job applications and interviews, report writing, and public speaking.
notes: Originally at openpress.usask.ca/rcm200 (now redirects to saskoer.ca). Editors: Rebekah Bennetch and Zachary Keesey.

title: Writing for Digital Media
summary: Digital writing text organized around critical, rhetorical, and functional literacies for composing in web and social media environments.
notes: Print edition available. Table of contents organized in three parts (Critical Literacy, Rhetorical Literacy, Functional Literacy).

title: Leveraging Data Visualization to Communicate Effectively
summary: Open text on choosing, designing, and presenting data visualizations so that they communicate clearly to business and general audiences.
notes: ISBN 9781956390476 (per Open Textbook Library). Chapter list not reviewed in detail.

title: Professional Writing and Communications for Business
summary: Business writing text organized as insights, information, implementation, and interface (professional voice), closing with integrity and generative AI in business communication and a section on teamwork and leadership.
notes: Year from the Open Textbook Library listing (book metadata left the year blank).

title: Communicating Strategically in the Workplace: A Resource for Engineering and Science Majors
authors: Chatterjee, Karishma; Ricks, Damla; Waryas Hughey, Diane E.
publisher_platform: Mavs Open Press (University of Texas at Arlington)
summary: Technical and professional communication text for engineering and science majors covering interpersonal and mediated communication, teamwork, culture, invention strategies, language, routine and bad-news messages, presentations, reports and proposals, employment documents, and citation.
notes: ISBN 9781648160202 (per Open Textbook Library).

title: Business Writing Style Guide
summary: Compact style guide for business students on clear, concise business writing at the sentence and document level.
notes: Open Textbook Library lists copyright year 2020; book metadata says 2018.

title: Technical Writing for Technicians
publisher_platform: Linn-Benton Community College / Open Oregon Pressbooks
summary: Ten-week technical writing course for career and technical education students, pairing workplace genres (emails, intake documents, instructions, bad-news messages, project completion reports, technical descriptions, resumes, cover letters) with short grammar lessons.
notes: Includes a set of sample documents. ISBN 9781636350097 (per Open Textbook Library).

title: Thinking Rhetorically: Writing for Professional and Public Audiences
authors: Roger Williams University Department of Writing Studies, Rhetoric, and Composition
summary: Roger Williams University reader for a professional and public writing course that applies rhetorical thinking to writing for workplace and civic audiences.
notes: Based on rwu.pressbooks.pub/wtng225. Table of contents not reviewed in detail.

title: Business Communication: Five Core Competencies
authors: Lucas, Kristen; Rawlins, Jacob D.; Haugen, Jenna
publisher_platform: State Assisted Academic Library Council of Kentucky (SAALCK)
summary: Business communication text organized around five competencies: being professional, clear, concise, evidence-driven, and persuasive.
notes: Chapters: Becoming Competent; Professional; Clear; Concise; Evidence-Driven; Persuasive; Afterword.

title: The Discipline of Organizing: 4th Professional Edition
summary: Interdisciplinary treatment of how people and systems organize information and resources, drawing on library science, information architecture, and computing; useful background for information architecture and content modeling.
notes: Open Textbook Library lists copyright year 2013 for the original work; this Pressbooks professional edition is dated 2020.

title: Information Strategies for Communicators
summary: Research text for students in journalism, public relations, and advertising on finding, evaluating, and using information for professional communication.

title: Graphic Design and Print Production Fundamentals
summary: Introduction to graphic design principles, typography, colour, layout, and the print production workflow; useful background for document design units.

title: Technical Project Management in Living and Geometric Order (Third Edition)
authors: Russell, Jeffrey S.; Pferdehirt, Wayne P.; Nelson, John S.
summary: Engineering project management text on planning, organizing, and leading technical projects, including stakeholder communication and team practices.

title: Communication and Teamwork Skills to Support Neurodiversity
authors: Menhenett, Teagan; Milne, Nick; Krishnan, Siva
summary: Guide to communication and teamwork practices that support neurodivergent students and colleagues in study and workplace teams.
notes: Editor: Teagan Menhenett.

title: Workplace Writing: A Handbook for Common Workplace Genres and Professional Writing
publisher_platform: New Prairie Press (Kansas State University Libraries)
summary: Handbook for a general business writing course with descriptions and discussion of common routine and formal workplace genres in print and electronic forms.
notes: ISBN 978-1-944548-00-1. The original New Prairie Press URL (newprairiepress.org/ebooks/8/) now redirects to Fulcrum.

title: Grant Writing: The Essentials
publisher_platform: Rod Library, University of Northern Iowa (OEN Manifold)
summary: Introductory guide to grant writing for students in nonprofit management, research, and related fields, covering how to find funding and plan and write competitive proposals.
notes: Rights holder Jayme Renfro. Google Doc versions are linked from the Open Textbook Library record.

title: Intercultural Communication
summary: Adapted open text on culture as a variable in interpersonal and collective communication, examining how differences in communication patterns, processes, and codes create opportunities and problems across cultural groups.
notes: UMSL OER adaptation; minor revisions uploaded 2024 and October 2026.

title: Writing Spaces Web Writing Style Guide, Version 1.0
authors: Barton, Matt; Kalmbach, James; Lowe, Charles (eds.)
summary: Crowdsourced guide by college writing teachers on composing for the web, covering online style, linking, multimedia, and design choices for web texts.
notes: Created at Collaborvention 2011 (Computers and Writing unconference). Dated but still useful as a short reading on web style.

title: Design Discourse: Composing and Revising Programs in Professional and Technical Writing
authors: Franke, David; Reid, Alex; Di Renzo, Anthony (eds.)
summary: Edited collection on building and revising professional and technical writing programs, with case studies of curricula and program design.
notes: Chapter PDFs available individually from the WAC Clearinghouse page. No derivatives permitted.

title: Handbook for Mindful Technical Writing: A Practical Guide for University Students and Professionals (2026 Edition)
publisher_platform: Montana Technological University (Digital Commons @ Montana Tech)
summary: Practical handbook distilled from the authors' advanced-level writing textbook, giving students and professionals quick guidance on technical, business, and scientific writing tasks.
notes: License discrepancy: the Montana Tech repository page shows CC BY-SA 4.0; the Open Textbook Library listing says CC BY-NC-SA. Check the PDF's own notice before remixing.

title: Mindful Technical Writing: An Introduction to the Fundamentals (2026 Edition)
publisher_platform: Montana Technological University (Digital Commons @ Montana Tech)
summary: Modular open textbook for corequisite pairings of developmental writing and introductory technical writing, with chapters and built-in activities instructors can assign selectively.
notes: First edition 2021 (digitalcommons.mtech.edu/writing/3/). License discrepancy: repository page shows CC BY-SA 4.0; Open Textbook Library lists CC BY-NC-SA for the 2026 edition.

title: Advanced-Level Writing in the University Classroom and Beyond: Mindful Practices for Technical, Business, and Scientific Communication (2026 Edition)
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (per Open Textbook Library listing)
summary: All-in-one upper-division text on technical, business, and scientific writing and technical editing, from Montana Tech's writing faculty.
notes: License taken from the Open Textbook Library record; not confirmed in the PDF this session. The companion Handbook and Mindful Technical Writing show CC BY-SA 4.0 on Montana Tech's repository, so this book may carry the same license.

title: Understanding Document Accessibility: A Reference for Creating Accessible Office Documents
authors: Digital Education Strategies, The Chang School
summary: Reference for creating accessible word-processed documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and PDFs, reviewing the accessibility tools in common authoring applications.
notes: Editor: Pauline Ricablanca. Formerly at pressbooks.library.ryerson.ca/docs/.

title: Digital Accessibility as a Business Practice: Essential Skills for Business Leaders
authors: Digital Education Strategies, The Chang School
summary: Guide for managers on building digital accessibility into an organization through culture change, awareness, and equipping employees with everyday accessibility skills.
notes: Formerly at pressbooks.library.ryerson.ca/dabp/.

authors: Digital Education Strategies, The Chang School
summary: Teaches how to evaluate websites and web content against WCAG 2, covering automated review tools, manual testing strategies, and writing up audit reports.
notes: Formerly at pressbooks.library.ryerson.ca/pwaa/.

title: Web Accessibility for Developers: Essential Skills for Web Developers
authors: Digital Education Strategies, The Chang School
summary: Technical resource for programmers on building accessible web interactivity with WAI-ARIA so that assistive technologies such as screen readers work well.
notes: Editor: Pauline Ricablanca. More developer-focused than most writing-course readings.

authors: Kinonen, Amber; Mold, Joseph; Erickson, Edie; Curtin, Shawn
